speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start by clarifying the nature of your pain: is the swelling and pain in your left knee constant, or does it flare up at certain times of the day? Additionally, have you noticed any redness, warmth, or a change in the color of the skin over the affected area?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old male. The patient reports increasing pain and swelling of the left knee over 2 months. Describes the pain as severe enough to awaken him from sleep on several occasions. States he tried taking ibuprofen with no relief. No family or personal history of significant illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pain waking you from sleep is significant; does the knee feel warm or look redder compared to your right side, and is there any history of similar episodes in the past? REQUEST TEST: ESR, CRP, Rheumatoid_Factor, HLA-B27

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Erythrocyte_Sedimentation_Rate: Slightly elevated; C-Reactive_Protein: Within normal limits; Rheumatoid_Factor: Not available in current data; HLA-B27: Not available in current data

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe pain and swelling in the left knee. I also have Pain intensifying over 2 months, Painful awakenings during night, No relief with ibuprofen.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Engineer by profession.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent fevers, weight loss, trauma to the knee, or previous similar episodes. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is highly unusual, as a urinary tract infection would not cause isolated knee swelling and night pain; we must investigate this as an inflammatory or crystal-induced joint issue instead. Can you tell me if you have a history of gout, psoriasis, or eye inflammation, and do you experience any back or hip stiffness? REQUEST TEST: Uric_Acid, X-Ray_Knee_Left
REQUEST IMAGES: X-Ray_Knee_Left

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Uric_Acid: Not available in current data; X-Ray_Left_Knee: A lytic lesion in the distal femur near the knee joint with a thin rim of bone on the external surface and a 'soap bubble' appearance.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Giant Cell Tumor of the Bone. This "soap bubble" lytic lesion in the distal femur of a young adult with night pain and swelling is classic for this condition; please avoid any invasive procedures due to fracture risk.
